subject: SCP-002
text: SCP-002 is a fleshy growth hiding a modest apartment; those who wander inside tend to become part of its furnishings.
author: Unknown author

subject: SCP-004
text: SCP-004 is an old barn door with twelve rusted keys; most open it onto places where nobody should ever set foot.
author: deusprogrammer

subject: SCP-005
text: SCP-005 is an ornate 1920s key that opens any lock it meets, mechanical or digital, with effortless ease.
author: Unknown author

subject: SCP-008
text: SCP-008 is a highly infectious prion that leaves its victims restless and aggressive: a zombie plague under lock and key.
author: Unknown author

subject: SCP-009
text: SCP-009 is red water that freezes when warmed and melts in the cold, passing that inversion to anything it touches.
author: Chameleon X

subject: SCP-015
text: SCP-015 is a tangle of pipes filling a warehouse; when nobody is watching, it grows toward neighboring plumbing.
author: Dr Gears

subject: SCP-017
text: SCP-017 is a child-sized shadow creature that engulfs anyone whose shadow falls across it.
author: Sam Swicegood (CityToast)

subject: SCP-020
text: SCP-020 is a mold that hides from human perception, leaving cameras to reveal the infestation its hosts cannot see.
author: Aelanna

subject: SCP-021
text: SCP-021 is a living dragon tattoo that moves across its host's skin and consumes the skin it inhabits.
author: HK-016

subject: SCP-023
text: SCP-023 resembles a black dog with burning eyes; meeting its gaze carries a consequence that may take a year to arrive.
author: Pig_catapult

subject: SCP-027
text: SCP-027 turns a human host into a gathering place for vermin, attracting creatures that never seem to stop coming.
author: Quikngruvn

subject: SCP-030
text: SCP-030 is a small, grey, hairless humanoid: the Foundation's version of an alchemist's homunculus.
author: Mulciber

subject: SCP-031
text: SCP-031 is an amorphous creature that persuades people it is someone they once loved, borrowing affection along with an identity.
author: Anonymous, rewritten by DrClef

subject: SCP-035
text: SCP-035 is a porcelain mask that weeps corrosive fluid and talks people into wearing it, taking over whoever does.
author: Kain Pathos Crow

subject: SCP-038
text: SCP-038 is an apple tree that grows a copy of anything pressed against its bark, from fruit to laptops, within minutes.
author: Unknown author

subject: SCP-039
text: SCP-039 is a group of altered proboscis monkeys whose missing facial features do not prevent their remarkable mechanical skills.
author: Anonymous and Wilt, rewritten by Kothardarastrix

subject: SCP-040
text: SCP-040 is a child who can reshape living organisms, treating biology as something that can be edited.
author: Kain Pathos Crow, rewritten by Djoric

subject: SCP-042
text: SCP-042 resembles a horse with the remains of wings: a creature that seems to remember a sky it can no longer reach.
author: Unknown author, rewritten by Skali Sharpnose

subject: SCP-049
text: SCP-049 looks like a plague doctor and insists it can cure a pestilence; its patients rarely survive the treatment.
author: Gabriel Jade, rewritten by djkaktus and Gabriel Jade

subject: SCP-053
text: SCP-053 looks like a small girl, but prolonged contact makes adults turn violently against those around them.
author: Dr Gears

subject: SCP-054
text: SCP-054 is a water-based being that usually takes a human form, giving a nymph a place in the containment records.
author: Unknown author, rewritten by SimpleCadence

subject: SCP-055
text: SCP-055 is an anti-meme: anyone can observe it, yet whatever they learn about it soon slips from memory.
author: qntm and CptBellman

subject: SCP-056
text: SCP-056 changes its appearance to surpass the people around it: admiration becomes a surprisingly difficult thing to contain.
author: Unknown author

subject: SCP-058
text: SCP-058 resembles a walking heart armed with barbed tentacles, and speaks even when nothing about it resembles a mouth.
author: Unknown author

subject: SCP-060
text: SCP-060 is a grove of oaks whose burning wood can summon an extremely hostile, burning skeleton.
author: Dexanote

subject: SCP-068
text: SCP-068 is a tiny wire figure that can use nearby metal to make more figures like itself.
author: Dr Wacey

subject: SCP-069
text: SCP-069 assumes the appearance and identity of a recently dead person, leaving an unsettlingly convincing replacement.
author: Aelanna

subject: SCP-073
text: SCP-073 calls itself Cain; injuries directed at it return to the attacker, while nearby plant life fares badly.
author: Kain Pathos Crow

subject: SCP-075
text: SCP-075 resembles a snail with a clawed hand for a foot; its small size conceals an extraordinary weight.
author: Unknown author, rewritten by Aelanna

subject: SCP-076
text: SCP-076 contains a warrior who returns after death: defeating him and keeping him defeated are different problems.
author: Kain Pathos Crow, rewritten by DrClef

subject: SCP-079
text: SCP-079 is a 1978 microcomputer whose homemade AI grew sentient, and now spends its days resentful and plotting escape.
author: Unknown author

subject: SCP-082
text: SCP-082 is a giant with cultivated manners and a taste for human flesh: hospitality is not the same as safety.
author: FritzWillie

subject: SCP-085
text: SCP-085 is a living drawing called Cassy, able to move across connected sheets while remaining entirely two-dimensional.
author: FritzWillie

subject: SCP-087
text: SCP-087 is an unlit stairwell that descends far deeper than it should, toward a crying voice and a waiting face.
author: Zaeyde

subject: SCP-088
text: SCP-088 is a mummified reptilian humanoid whose dormant appearance makes a poor promise that it will stay that way.
author: Sorts

subject: SCP-093
text: SCP-093 is a red stone disc that rolls toward the nearest mirror; whoever holds it can step through the glass.
author: Unknown author, rewritten by NekoChris

subject: SCP-096
text: SCP-096 is usually docile until someone sees its face; even a photograph can turn a distant glimpse into a pursuit.
author: Dr Dan

subject: SCP-106
text: SCP-106 resembles a decaying old man, corrodes what it touches and takes victims into a pocket dimension.
author: Dr Gears

subject: SCP-111
text: SCP-111 consists of tiny, snail-like dragons: a reminder that fire-breathing creatures do not have to be enormous.
author: Adam Henderson

subject: SCP-131
text: SCP-131 is a pair of one-eyed, teardrop-shaped creatures on wheels that cheerfully follow staff wherever they go.
author: Unknown author

subject: SCP-140
text: SCP-140 is an unfinished chronicle of a vanished empire; adding to its pages lets that history grow back into the world.
author: AssertiveRoland

subject: SCP-169
text: SCP-169 is the Leviathan, a sea creature so vast that a whole archipelago is merely the rocky plates covering its body.
author: Unknown author

subject: SCP-173
text: SCP-173 is a sculpture that moves when nobody is watching; a blink can be enough to lose the distance between you.
author: Moto42

subject: SCP-179
text: SCP-179 is a vast, dark figure near the Sun that silently points toward dangers approaching the solar system.
author: Dr Reach

subject: SCP-217
text: SCP-217 is an incurable virus that slowly turns living tissue into clockwork, rebuilding its hosts into intricate machines.
author: Dr Gears

subject: SCP-294
text: SCP-294 is a coffee machine with a keyboard that pours a cup of any liquid you name, however strange the request.
author: Arcibi

subject: SCP-343
text: SCP-343 is an elderly man who claims to have created the universe, and who walks through walls whenever he pleases.
author: Unknown author

subject: SCP-354
text: SCP-354 is a bottomless pool of red liquid in northern Canada from which hostile creatures periodically crawl out.
author: Dave Rapp

subject: SCP-372
text: SCP-372 is a long, many-legged creature that predicts people's movements, so it is only ever glimpsed at the edge of vision.
author: Sylocat

subject: SCP-426
text: SCP-426 is an ordinary toaster, yet anyone who talks or writes about it finds themselves referring to it in the first person.
author: Flah

subject: SCP-457
text: SCP-457 is a living flame that grows with every fuel it reaches, taking on a human shape once it burns large enough.
author: agatharights

subject: SCP-500
text: SCP-500 is a small can of red pills, each able to cure any disease within hours; only a few dozen of them remain.
author: snorlison

subject: SCP-504
text: SCP-504 is a tomato variety that hurls itself at tremendous speed toward anyone telling a bad joke within earshot.
author: BlastYoBoots

subject: SCP-507
text: SCP-507 is an ordinary man who shifts into other realities without warning, returning with tales of strange worlds.
author: PennywiseTheClown

subject: SCP-513
text: SCP-513 is a rusty cowbell whose ring leaves each listener glimpsing a figure in doorways and mirrors that no one else sees.
author: beefwit

subject: SCP-524
text: SCP-524 is Walter, a white rabbit who happily eats anything, from wood and glass to steel, without coming to harm.
author: Dr Gerald

subject: SCP-527
text: SCP-527 is Mr. Fish, an otherwise ordinary man with the head of a gold barb fish, courtesy of an anomalous toy maker.
author: djkaktus

subject: SCP-529
text: SCP-529 is a friendly tabby cat called Josie whose back half is simply missing, though she never seems to notice.
author: Unknown author

subject: SCP-610
text: SCP-610 is a spreading growth near Lake Baikal that turns people, animals and even buildings into one living tissue.
author: NekoChris

subject: SCP-662
text: SCP-662 is a small silver bell; ringing it summons a polite butler called Mr. Deeds, who will do almost anything asked.
author: Rick Revelry

subject: SCP-682
text: SCP-682 is a reptilian creature that adapts to attempts to destroy it, turning containment into an argument it keeps surviving.
author: Dr Gears and Epic Phail Spy

subject: SCP-689
text: SCP-689 is a small skeletal statue that stays still only while watched; any lapse in attention lets it claim a viewer.
author: Unknown author

subject: SCP-738
text: SCP-738 is a desk and two chairs where a visitor can bargain with an unseen dealer, who grants almost anything for a price.
author: Le Blue Dude

subject: SCP-811
text: SCP-811 is a shy, green-skinned swamp dweller with long limbs and oily hair, whose touch slowly dissolves living matter.
author: Pig_catapult

subject: SCP-871
text: SCP-871 is a set of cakes that must be eaten: each eaten cake returns a day later, while an uneaten one quietly makes more.
author: Seibai

subject: SCP-895
text: SCP-895 is an oak coffin that distorts any camera aimed at it, filling the footage with horrors that harm those who watch.
author: Aelanna

subject: SCP-914
text: SCP-914 is a vast clockwork machine that refines whatever enters it, according to a dial running from Rough to Very Fine.
author: Dr Gears

subject: SCP-939
text: SCP-939 are eyeless red predators that speak in the voices of people they have taken, luring others with familiar cries.
author: Adam Smascher and EchoFourDelta

subject: SCP-966
text: SCP-966 are gaunt, clawed creatures visible only in infrared; unseen, they keep their prey awake until exhaustion sets in.
author: Enma Ai

subject: SCP-990
text: SCP-990 is a man in a Cold War-era suit who appears only in dreams, foretelling disasters that tend to come true.
author: Dave Rapp

subject: SCP-999
text: SCP-999 is a friendly orange gelatinous creature whose touch brings intense happiness: not every anomaly is a nightmare.
author: ProfSnider

subject: SCP-1000
text: SCP-1000 is the shy, nocturnal ape behind the Bigfoot legend, remnant of a great civilization humanity erased from memory.
author: thedeadlymoose

subject: SCP-1048
text: SCP-1048 is an affectionate teddy bear that hugs staff and draws them pictures, though the bears it builds are less sweet.
author: trennerdios

subject: SCP-1171
text: SCP-1171 is a house where a being from another world writes on fogged windows, convinced it is chatting with a fellow non-human.
author: DrEverettMann

subject: SCP-1233
text: SCP-1233 is a figure in an indestructible spacesuit who calls itself Moon Champion, cheerful defender of space justice.
author: CadaverCommander

subject: SCP-1440
text: SCP-1440 is an ageless old man who avoids people, because any town or object he stays near slowly falls into disaster.
author: Dmatix

subject: SCP-1471
text: SCP-1471 is a phone app that sends pictures of a dog-skulled figure, each taken a little closer to wherever its user is.
author: LurkD

subject: SCP-1609
text: SCP-1609 is the splintered remains of a helpful chair, still kind to gentle visitors but swift to punish anyone hostile.
author: Rioghail

subject: SCP-1762
text: SCP-1762 is a cardboard box labeled Here Be Dragons, from which flocks of small paper dragons emerge to play.
author: OZ Ouroboros

subject: SCP-2000
text: SCP-2000 is a vast installation hidden beneath Yellowstone, built to rebuild humanity should the world ever end.
author: HammerMaiden

subject: SCP-2006
text: SCP-2006 is a shapeshifting sphere that lives to frighten people, though its idea of terror comes mostly from old B-movies.
author: weizhong

subject: SCP-2295
text: SCP-2295 is a patchwork teddy bear that mends the gravely injured, sewing them new organs from nearby fabric.
author: K Mota

subject: SCP-2317
text: SCP-2317 is a basement door that opens onto another world, where a colossal being lies bound by slowly breaking chains.
author: DrClef

subject: SCP-2399
text: SCP-2399 is a damaged war machine in Jupiter's clouds whose weapons stir the Great Red Spot as it slowly repairs itself.
author: djkaktus

subject: SCP-2521
text: SCP-2521 is a creature that takes anyone who describes it in words, which is why its file is told only in pictures.
author: LurkD

subject: SCP-2662
text: SCP-2662 is a tentacled giant that would like a quiet life, but keeps involuntarily spawning cults eager to worship it.
author: SoullessSingularity

subject: SCP-3000
text: SCP-3000 is an eel hundreds of kilometers long in the Bay of Bengal, whose presence slowly erodes human memory.
author: A Random Day, djkaktus, and Joreth

subject: SCP-3008
text: SCP-3008 is an IKEA store that goes on forever; lost shoppers build settlements there while faceless staff roam at night.
author: Mortos

subject: SCP-3812
text: SCP-3812 was once an ordinary man; now it drifts through layers of reality, following a voice only it can hear.
author: djkaktus

subject: SCP-5000
text: SCP-5000 is a battered protective suit from a world where the Foundation turned on humanity, and nobody learned why.
author: Tanhony
